title: fix(plugins): repair stale host packages after OpenClaw upgrades

commit.messageHeadline: fix(plugins): repair stale registered host package links
refactor(plugins): isolate authoritative host-link repair owners
fix(plugins): constrain host repair to registered install roots

Codex review: needs maintainer review before merge. _Reviewed August 2, 2026, 8:43 PM ET / August 3, 2026, 00:43 UTC._ # ClawSweeper review ## What this changes Repairs stale nested `openclaw` host packages for registered npm plugins during Doctor, plugin updates, and post-core-update convergence without touching developer-owned or out-of-root installations. ## Merge readiness ⚠️ **Ready for maintainer review - 3 items remain** Keep open. Current main repairs host links only inside managed npm project roots, while this PR adds the missing registered legacy `state/extensions/<pluginId>` repair path and resolves the prior arbitrary-path mutation finding with exact record, root, and realpath checks. The protected `maintainer` label and upgrade-time filesystem mutation still require a maintainer security-boundary decision before landing. **Priority:** P1 **Reviewed head:** `c7547e2d7f68765d09e25a7cc2c8ba75a0697669` **Owner decision:** Required. See [Decision needed](#decision-needed). ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | The patch has focused source and ownership-boundary coverage plus reported real-install proof; the remaining gate is maintainer acceptance of automatic legacy-state repair semantics. | | **Proof confidence** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | Sufficient (live_output): The PR body provides after-fix real packaged npm-install evidence and states that the final head exercised two real local-registry installs plus filesystem repair scenarios; redact private paths or registry details if additional evidence is posted. | | **Patch quality** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | No actionable review findings were identified. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Verified | Sufficient (live_output): The PR body provides after-fix real packaged npm-install evidence and states that the final head exercised two real local-registry installs plus filesystem repair scenarios; redact private paths or registry details if additional evidence is posted. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 7 items | Current-main gap: Current main's post-core convergence repairs only managed npm project roots via `relinkOpenClawPeerDependenciesInManagedNpmRoot`; it has no registered extensions-root reconciliation, so the reported legacy install remains uncovered.
Canonical repair boundary: The PR accepts only npm records whose resolved install path exactly equals the plugin-id-derived directory, whose realpath stays inside the extensions root, and whose realpath is exactly the expected path before it can inspect or relink a host dependency.
Post-update owner uses the constrained reconciler: The PR routes legacy registered installs through the same constrained reconciler before the active-plugin payload smoke check, while retaining the existing managed-npm-root repair path. | | **Findings** | None | None. | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together OpenClaw stores installed-plugin records in its state index and loads plugin packages from managed roots. Doctor and update convergence inspect those records, repair a stale plugin-local host package when the installation is proven to be OpenClaw-managed, then run payload checks before the gateway uses the plugin. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Installed plugin index] --> B[Registered npm install record] B --> C[Exact extensions-root and realpath checks] C --> D[Inspect package host dependency] D --> E[Repair stale nested OpenClaw host link] E --> F[Doctor or update convergence] F --> G[Payload smoke check] G --> H[Gateway loads healthy plugin] ``` ## Decision needed | Question | Recommendation | |---|---| | Does the exact registered npm record plus expected extensions-root realpath predicate provide the intended authorization boundary for replacing a stale nested `openclaw` package during Doctor and update repair? | **Confirm the constrained repair boundary:** Accept repair only for authoritative npm records at their exact canonical extensions-root path, then merge after normal current-head checks complete. | Why: The patch performs destructive repair of user-local plugin directories; source review shows the requested narrowing, but repository policy reserves larger ownership and security-boundary changes for maintainer judgment, and Codex-specific source validation could not be completed locally. ## Before merge - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - This intentionally changes upgrade-time filesystem repair: a stale copied nested `openclaw` directory may be replaced with a canonical host link, so maintainers must accept the exact registered-root and realpath predicate as the ownership boundary. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - The affected report concerns the Codex plugin, but the sibling Codex checkout required by repository policy was unavailable and GitHub DNS prevented obtaining it; the remaining Codex-specific runtime contract check needs an environment with that source available.

Confirm migration or upgrade compatibility proof before merge. ### Root-cause cluster Relationship: `fixed_by_candidate` Canonical: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/108705 Summary: This PR is a concrete candidate repair for the open stale-host-package regression described in the linked issue; current main still lacks the registered legacy-install repair path. Members: - `canonical`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/108705 - The PR body uses closing linkage and its source change targets the stale nested host-package failure described there. Proposal only: this assessment does not dispatch repair, suppress jobs, mutate sibling items, close, or merge anything. ### Merge-risk options **Maintainer options:** 1. **Confirm exact-root repair semantics before merge (recommended)** Accept the upgrade repair only if maintainers agree that a registered npm record plus canonical root and realpath checks establishes OpenClaw ownership of the nested host package. 2. **Keep repair explicit-only** If automatic replacement is too broad for legacy installations, narrow the change to Doctor's explicit repair path and document the operator-visible recovery. ### Technical review Best possible solution: Land the canonical SQLite-record and exact-realpath repair only after a maintainer confirms that registered npm installs at the exact `state/extensions/` path are OpenClaw-owned upgrade state and accepts the bounded replacement behavior. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Yes, source reproducibly shows the gap: current main repairs managed npm project roots but not registered legacy npm installs under the extensions root; the PR adds focused filesystem regressions for that state. Is this the best way to solve the issue? Yes, subject to the maintainer ownership decision: routing all legacy repair paths through the SQLite-record-derived exact-root reconciler is safer than the earlier arbitrary install-path loop and keeps developer-owned installs out of scope.
